chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who has two wives, one of whom is more beloved to him than the other. He said to him: He may come to her for three nights and to the other for one night. But if he wishes to marry four women, then each woman has one night. Therefore, he may give preference to some of them over others so long as they are not four.

key_terms.أَحَبُّ: more beloved or preferred in affection
key_terms.لَيْلَةً: one night as an allotted turn

ai.seo_question: How should a husband divide nights between his wives according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the division of nights between wives in marriage. It indicates that when a man has fewer than four wives, he may show some preference in allotting nights, but when they are four, each wife is entitled to one night.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4482 - Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who has two wives, one of whom is more beloved to him than the other. Imam (as) said: "He may spend three nights with her and one night with the other. However, if he wishes to marry four wives, then each wife is entitled to one night. Therefore, it is permissible for him to prefer some of them over others as long as they are not four."
